title: Beyond the Margin: Targeted Conservation and Household Water Demand
abstract: arXiv:2606.23347v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Non-price interventions targeting specific household water uses are increasingly central to conservation policy, but whether end-use savings translate into lower aggregate demand remains unclear. This paper reports evidence from a pre-registered field experiment in which 775 Finnish households were randomized to a shower timer, a water-saving shower head, or the same shower head with real-time feedback. Utility-grade water meters measure household-level effects, while shower-level data provide complementary end-use evidence for the two shower-head treatments. The shower timer has no detectable effect. In contrast, the water-saving shower head reduces daily household demand by about 5%, and pairing it with real-time feedback doubles this reduction to about 10%. translated_title: 超越边缘：针对性保护与家庭用水需求
translated_abstract: arXiv:2606.23347v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：针对特定家庭用水用途的非价格干预措施日益成为保护政策的核心，但终端使用节约是否转化为更低的总需求仍不清楚。本文报告了一项预注册的现场实验证据，其中775个芬兰家庭被随机分配至淋浴计时器、节水淋浴头或配备实时反馈的同一淋浴头。公用事业级水表测量家庭层面的效果，而淋浴层面数据为两种淋浴头处理提供补充的终端使用证据。淋浴计时器没有可检测的效果。相比之下，节水淋浴头将每日家庭需求减少约5%，而将其与实时反馈配对则使这一减少翻倍至约10%。淋浴和基于水表的估计之间的收敛表明，终端使用节约与家庭其他地方的有限抵消一致。成本效益分析表明...
tldr: 该研究通过预注册现场实验发现，节水淋浴头可减少家庭用水需求约5%，结合实时反馈可增至10%，且终端节约与整体需求减少一致，具有显著成本效益。
en_tdlr: This study, via a pre-registered field experiment, finds that water-saving shower heads reduce household water demand by about 5%, doubling to 10% with real-time feedback, with end-use savings consistent with overall demand reduction and significant cost-effectiveness.
